python_url_components.observed: urlparse exposes scheme, netloc, path, query, fragment, username, password, hostname and port separately; invalid port access raises ValueError.

python_request_selector.observed: Request preserves full_url/fragment separately and derives selector from the request target, so fragment/query/path differences must not be collapsed by provider identity bookkeeping.

http_402.observed: HTTP 402 Payment Required remains reserved for future use; nonretryable FREE_ONLY treatment is therefore a local cost-safety policy, not generic RFC semantics.

hypothesis.statement: A FREE_ONLY provider execution must bind an exact provider-owned operation capability plus a budget-epoch cost-policy principal before credentials are attached, and any observed HTTP 402 must latch that provider out of the same budget epoch as a nonretryable hard stop.
hypothesis.strongest_counterhypothesis: Origin-level scheme/host/port binding plus transient cooldown is sufficient because same-origin alternate paths either fail harmlessly and 402 has no standard retry semantics.
hypothesis.discriminator: Same-origin path/query/fragment aliases must be denied before opener invocation; regular-response and HTTPError 402 paths must both set a latch, emit retryable=false and prevent a second request in the same budget epoch while allowing a separately identified new epoch.

out_of_box_experiment.name: URL_ENDPOINT_METAMORPHIC_IDENTITY_MATRIX
out_of_box_experiment.method: Compare raw and current-rstrip URL parsing plus urllib Request full_url/selector across canonical, trailing-slash, repeated-slash, uppercase-host, explicit-443, dot-segment, percent-encoded-path, query, fragment and double-slash variants.
material_findings: Current pre-parse rstrip('/') collapses /v1/// into canonical /v1 before identity inspection.
Query and fragment variants produce materially different full_url/selector behavior while the prior request_id bound only provider hostname plus body digest.

Uppercase host and explicit default port are semantically equivalent after parsed hostname/effective-port normalization and can safely canonicalize to the provider-owned target after equivalence is established.

changes: Parse raw provider base URL before trailing-slash normalization.
For remote execution require canonical provider scheme/hostname/effective-port/path and empty params/query/fragment before credential attachment.
Construct remote request from provider-owned canonical base after equivalence validation.
Bind endpoint_capability_id, cost_policy_principal_id and budget_epoch_id into redacted receipts and logical request identity.
Introduce injectable/shared budget-epoch payment latch state; default process-local state remains available without creating a second persistent semantic store.
Classify HTTP 402 in both ordinary-response and HTTPError paths as payment_required_hard_stop with retryable=false and cooldown_seconds=0.
Prevent subsequent provider selection inside the same budget epoch after a 402 latch.
implementation_delta.important_boundary: The new latch supports externally persisted/shared latch state but its default is process-local. Durable cross-restart same-budget-epoch enforcement still requires UnifiedDB/runtime integration evidence before release credit.

counterevidence_and_surviving_blockers: RFC 9110 does not standardize 402 retry or payment semantics; the hard stop is project policy and needs its own acceptance evidence.
cost_policy_principal_id binds provider/key-name/evidence-class/budget-epoch but does not prove an external provider account/billing principal; account identity remains unresolved.
Default payment latch lifetime is process-local; durable UnifiedDB/restart continuity is not yet proven.
